Bug_Title: Methods should not be named "tostring", "hashcode" or "equal"
Bug_Details:
Due to the similar name with the methods Object.toString , Object.hashCode and Object.equals , there is a
significant likelihood that a developer intended to override one of these methods but made a spelling error.
Even if no such error exists and the naming was done on purpose, these method names can be misleading. Readers might not notice the difference, or
if they do, they may falsely assume that the developer made a mistake.
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by intentionally naming three methods 'tostring', 'hashcode', and 'equal'. These method names are very similar to the standard Object class methods 'toString', 'hashCode', and 'equals', which can lead to confusion and potential errors.
Trigger_Explanation: The test triggers the bug by calling the showBug method, which internally calls the incorrectly named methods 'tostring', 'hashcode', and 'equal'. These method calls demonstrate the presence of the bug as the method names are intentionally misspelled to mimic the standard Object class methods.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test run results show that the test passed successfully without any errors or failures, indicating that the methods 'tostring', 'hashcode', and 'equal' were executed as expected and did not cause any issues that would indicate the presence of the bug.
